name: Goan Fish Curry Rice
description: Known locally as xitt-kodi, this is fish curry made with coconut, local spices and tangy kokum or tamarind, served with steamed rice. It is the everyday staple of Goa; the Hindu version is called humann.
how_to_eat: Pour the curry over the rice and eat it with a fried fish on the side.
how_to_order: Ask for a 'fish curry rice' or 'fish thali' at a local lunch place.

name: Ambot Tik
description: A spicy, sour Goan Catholic fish curry; jeerem-meerem is a milder, less sour version.
how_to_eat: Eat it with steamed rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'ambot tik' with shark or other fish at a Goan restaurant.

name: Xacuti
description: A curry with complex spicing, including white poppy seeds, toasted grated coconut and large dried red chillies, usually made with chicken, lamb, crab or beef. It is said to come from Harmal (Arambol) village in Pernem.
how_to_eat: Eat it with poi or pão bread, or with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chicken xacuti' at a Goan restaurant.

name: Vindalho
description: A spicy pork curry built on a garlic and vinegar marinade; the name comes from the Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos. The traditional Goan version has no potatoes, unlike the British 'vindaloo'.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or sanna; it tastes better the day after it is made.
how_to_order: Ask for 'pork vindalho' at a Goan home-style restaurant.

name: Sorpotel
description: A very spicy, vinegary dish of pork, Portuguese in origin, adapted by Goan Christians and made for feasts and Christmas. It is eaten with sanna or pão.
how_to_eat: Eat it with sanna or pão; like vindalho it improves over a few days.
how_to_order: Ask for 'sorpotel with sannas' at a Goan restaurant, especially around Christmas.

name: Chicken Cafreal
description: Chicken legs marinated in a green paste of coriander, green chillies, garlic, ginger, spices and lime juice or vinegar, then fried or roasted. It came to Goa through the Portuguese and African soldiers serving under them.
how_to_eat: Eat it with potato chips or bread and a wedge of lime.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chicken cafreal' at a Goan bar or restaurant.

name: Prawn Balchão
description: Fried fresh prawns pickled in a spicy, sour sauce of red chillies, tomato, garlic, ginger and vinegar. It can be made days ahead and served without reheating; fish and pork versions also exist.
how_to_eat: Eat a little with rice or bread; it is strong.
how_to_order: Ask for 'prawn balchão' at a Goan restaurant or buy it bottled.

name: Recheado Bangdo
description: Mackerel (bangdo) stuffed with recheado masala of red chillies, garlic, ginger and vinegar, then pan-fried until crisp. Pomfret is also cooked this way.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with rice and fish curry.
how_to_order: Ask for 'recheado mackerel' or 'pomfret recheado' at a Goan seafood restaurant.

name: Crab Xec Xec
description: A Goan crab curry, one of the classic dishes of Goan Catholic seafood cooking.
how_to_eat: Crack the shells by hand and eat with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'crab xec xec' at a Goan seafood restaurant.

name: Goan Sausage (Choris)
description: Pork pickled in vinegar, alcohol and a chilli-spice mix and stuffed into casings, based on the Portuguese chouriço. The pickling let it keep in Goa's humidity.
how_to_eat: Eat it fried with onions and potatoes, or as choris pão.
how_to_order: Ask for 'choris pão' (sausage bread) at a cafe or bakery stall.

name: Ros Omelette
description: An omelette drowned in ros, a spicy chicken or chickpea gravy similar to xacuti, served with pão. It is a Goan evening street food.
how_to_eat: Eat it with pão, mopping up the gravy.
how_to_order: Ask for 'ros omelette' at a roadside cart in the evening.

name: Bhaji Pão
description: A gravy of dried white peas with a dry potato bhaji, served hot with fresh Goan pão. It is a breakfast or evening snack.
how_to_eat: Dip the pão into the bhaji.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bhaji pão' at a local cafe in the morning.

name: Prawn Rissóis
description: A Portuguese-origin fried pastry filled with prawns. It stayed in Goan cooking after Portuguese rule ended.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot as a starter.
how_to_order: Ask for 'prawn rissóis' at a Goan restaurant or bakery.

name: Sanna
description: A spongy steamed savoury cake of rice, black lentil (urad) and coconut, similar to idli, made in the Konkan. It is traditionally the partner of sorpotel and other pork curries.
how_to_eat: Eat it with sorpotel or a spicy curry.
how_to_order: Ask for 'sannas' with sorpotel at a Goan restaurant, or buy them at markets around feasts.

name: Poi
description: A round leavened bread with a pocket, like pita, made from half refined and half whole-wheat flour by Goa's traditional bakers (paders). Toddy was traditionally used to ferment it.
how_to_eat: Eat it with curries, or split it and stuff it with sausage.
how_to_order: Buy 'poi' fresh in the morning from the pader's bicycle or a local bakery.

name: Khatkhate
description: A Goan Hindu stew of at least five vegetables with grated coconut, jaggery, kokum, tamarind, tirphal and spices. It is made for weddings, religious ceremonies and Ganesh Chaturthi.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice as part of a festive meal.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khatkhate' on a Goan Hindu (Saraswat) thali, especially around Ganesh Chaturthi.

name: Solkadhi
description: A pink drink of coconut milk and kokum, seasoned with salt and chilli-garlic paste, served chilled. It is drunk after spicy fish meals to aid digestion.
how_to_eat: Sip it chilled at the end of the meal.
how_to_order: Ask for 'sol kadi' with any fish thali.

name: Bebinca
description: Called the 'Queen of Goan desserts', a layer cake of flour, coconut milk, egg yolks, ghee and palm jaggery, with 7 to 16 layers each baked separately. It is a Christmas sweet but sold all year, and Goan Bebinca received a GI tag in 2023-24.
how_to_eat: Eat a thin slice at room temperature.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bebinca' by the slice or whole at a Goan bakery or sweet shop.

name: Goan Khaje
description: Finger-sized fried sticks of chickpea flour coated in jaggery with ginger and sesame, also called kaddio-boddio. They are sold at temple zatras and church feasts, and Goan Khaje has a GI tag.
how_to_eat: Snap and eat them as a crunchy snack.
how_to_order: Buy 'khaje' by weight from stalls at a zatra or church feast.

name: Patoleo
description: Turmeric leaves spread with rice-flour paste, filled with fresh coconut and palm jaggery, folded and steamed. Konkani Hindus make them for the second Sunday of Shravan, Nag Panchami and the eve of Ganesh Chaturthi.
how_to_eat: Unwrap the leaf and eat the filled rice layer warm.
how_to_order: Look for 'patoleo' in homes and at festive stalls around August.

name: Kulkul
description: Small shell-shaped curls of maida, milk and sometimes egg, fried in ghee or oil. They are part of kuswar, the Christmas sweets Goan Catholics make and exchange.
how_to_eat: Eat them by the handful as a crunchy snack.
how_to_order: Buy 'kulkuls' at bakeries or from home cooks in December.

name: Neureos
description: Sweet fried dumplings filled with coconut, sugar, poppy seeds, cardamom and almonds. They are a Christmas kuswar sweet.
how_to_eat: Eat one whole; it is crisp outside with a sweet filling.
how_to_order: Buy 'neureos' at bakeries or from home cooks in December.

name: Dodol
description: A dense, chewy sweet of coconut milk, palm jaggery and rice flour, cooked slowly until thick. It is part of the Goan Christmas kuswar.
how_to_eat: Eat it in thin slices.
how_to_order: Ask for 'dodol' at a Goan sweet shop or bakery around Christmas.

name: Serradura
description: A Portuguese dessert of layered whipped cream and finely crushed Marie biscuits; the name means 'sawdust'. It is popular in former Portuguese colonies including Goa.
how_to_eat: Eat it chilled with a spoon.
how_to_order: Ask for 'serradura' at Goan or Portuguese-style restaurants and cafes.

name: Feni
description: A spirit made in Goa, mainly from cashew apple or coconut sap, double-distilled to about 40-45% alcohol. Feni holds a GI tag; urrak is the lighter first-distillation spirit drunk in summer.
how_to_eat: Drink it neat in small sips or mixed with lime and soda.
how_to_order: Ask for 'cashew feni' or 'coconut feni' at a bar or licensed shop; adults only.
